Hi Gleice, this is Jennifer Lowe, the sales director of NatureCare Skin. Thank you for your interest in our partner page. I want to explain the job before our call. First, you don't have to be an employee of NatureCare. You work for yourself, and you receive a commission on every sale. We pay the commission every three months. Second, you have to visit at least twenty buyers every month, in pharmacy chains and distributors. Third, you have to send a short report about your visits every Friday. It is only one page. And finally, in September you have to come to Boston for one week of training. Don't worry, you don't have to pay for the trip. We pay for everything. Talk to you soon.

I have worked as a brand representative in pharmacies for fifteen years, and here is my advice. Before you sign an agreement, read it slowly, and check three things: the territory, the commission, and if it is exclusive. You don't have to accept the first offer. You can ask for a bigger territory or a better commission. Brands expect that. Then, when you start, remember one thing: the shelf is everything. If your product is not on the shelf at eye level, nobody buys it. So you have to visit the stores, not only the offices. And always take the catalog with you. Buyers have to see the products.

First, NatureCare says it wants to expand to Brazil. Then it explains that the distributor buys the products. After that, it says the agreement is exclusive for two years. Next, it says the representative receives a commission of eight percent. Finally, it says you have to send your plan by June thirtieth.
